title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, free on two generators, with loops l_0, l_1 (and l_∞). Ŝ^+_{0,3} is an extension of S_3 by Π̂_{0,3}; the next page states Π̂_{0,3} = Ker(Ŝ^+_{0,3} → S_3). It is the orbifold fundamental group of the S_3-quotient, the profinite analogue of the inclusion Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL_2(Z) with quotient S_3. It contains an element ε_0 with ε_0^2 = l_0 and an element σ_∞ of order 2 mapping to a transposition.

The map. φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a fixed homomorphism with φ̂(l_0) = ε_0 and φ̂(l_1) = σ_∞^{∓1} (up to sign conventions). Its composite with Ŝ^+ → S_3 sends l_0 and l_1 to transpositions.

The objects studied. These are elements u of a 'Teichmüller-type' automorphism set M̃^!_{0,3}. Each u is encoded by invariants of §46, in particular a triple (α, β, f) with:
- α ∈ Π̃^∧_{0,3} (a slightly larger group);
- β, f ∈ Π̂_{0,3};
- ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1} and η = β σ_∞ ρ(β)^{-1}, where ρ is the relevant involution.
The question is when u 'commutes exteriorly' with φ̂, i.e. is compatible with φ̂ up to inner automorphisms.

Previous page (Theorem). u commutes with φ̂ iff (7) holds: φ̂(ξ) = ε_0^r β σ_∞^i for some r ∈ Ẑ and i ∈ Z/2. The triple is defined only up to (8): (α, β, f) ↦ (l_0^n α, l_0^n β, l_0^n f), under which (9) holds: r' = r − n and i' = i + n mod 2.

This page (Corollary). Taking n = r makes r' = 0, and this choice of n is the only one doing so. Hence there is a unique 'normalized' triple satisfying the boxed relation (10): φ̂(ξ) = β σ_∞^i, with i ∈ Z/2.

Resulting bijection. The u commuting exteriorly with φ̂ correspond one-to-one to triples (α, β, f) satisfying two relations:
- the loop relation (11): ξ ≐ η l_1^ν, with ν ∈ Ẑ and 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ^× (the familiar parameter λ = 2ν+1 of GT-type theory);
- the normalization (10).
Neither relation involves f.

Margin note. The marginal note asks whether this definition coincides with an earlier one (pp. 41', 41'') up to a transformation of φ̂.

Next page. Projecting (10) to S_3 yields an intrinsic condition on ξ: modulo the normal subgroup generated by l_0^2, l_1^2, l_∞^3, ξ must be of the form l_1^i. This allows eliminating β and replacing α by ξ.

Purpose. The page is a bookkeeping step in Grothendieck's 'variations on the loop equation': parametrizing GT-like automorphisms compatible with an orbifold covering map, via the loop (hexagon-type) equation.
errors: No mathematical error. The uniqueness follows directly from (9): r' = r − n vanishes for exactly one n, namely n = r. The parity i is then determined.
The transcription's 'décrire φ̂ par un triple' should almost certainly read 'décrire u par un triple': it is u, not φ̂, that is described by (α, β, f).

ideas.what: Normalizing the triple (α, β, f) attached to an automorphism u by using the l_0^n-ambiguity (8) to kill the exponent r of ε_0 in (7), giving a canonical representative satisfying φ̂(ξ) = β σ_∞^i.
ideas.modern_name: normalization / gauge fixing of GT-type parameters (choice of section modulo a Ẑ-action)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard technique; GT-group parametrizations by Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1990s)

ideas.what: Characterizing automorphisms compatible (up to inner automorphisms) with the orbifold map Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} by the loop equation ξ ≐ η l_1^ν (with 2ν+1 a unit) plus a compatibility relation.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations for the S_3-orbifold quotient of M_{0,4} (compare GT relations involving PSL_2(Z)/Γ(2))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (GT and orbifold/modular compatibility)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and level 0/1 relations only in outline

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags but does not settle whether this normalized definition, based on exterior commutation with φ̂, agrees with an earlier definition (pp. 41', 41'') up to a transformation of φ̂. Whether the two parametrizations coincide is left open on this page.
missed.quote: Il faudrait examiner si cette définition coïncide avec celle de p. 41', 41'', à transformation φ̂ près
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a minor consistency check inside his own variant of the GT formalism. Its interest is mainly for reconstructing his notes, since the analogous compatibilities in the literature are settled by Drinfeld, Ihara and Nakamura.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine normalization step within Grothendieck's private development of GT-type loop equations. The underlying relations (loop equation with λ = 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ^×) are known from Drinfeld and Ihara. It is of historical interest only as part of his independent unpublished treatment.
transcription_corrections: 'décrire φ̂ par un triple' → probably 'décrire u par un triple' (the symbol after 'décrire' is a crossed-out letter; the object described is u).
The next page's 'i ∈ Z/12Z' is very likely a misreading of 'i ∈ Z/2Z', consistent with (10) here.
First line: 'Cela implique le' (followed by 'Corollaire!'), not 'la'.
Margin note, approximately: 'Il faudrait examiner si cette définition coïncide avec celles de p. 41', 41'', à transformation φ̂ près'.
